title: Distributed Affine Body Dynamics with Adaptive Consensus
abstract: Affine Body Dynamics (ABD) within the Incremental Potential Contact (IPC) framework provides accurate simulation of extremely stiff, near-rigid solids with strict non-penetration guarantees. However, IPC's globally coupled barrier constraints hinder scalable execution across multiple GPUs and compute nodes. This paper proposes a distributed formulation of ABD using a consensus-based ADMM scheme. Each compute node solves its local ABD subproblem in parallel, followed by a global consensus step that enforces consistency among shared boundary bodies. A mass-aware initialization of the ADMM penalty parameter combined with residual-driven adaptation accelerates convergence (22%-80% fewer iterations), and a feasibility-preserving consensus mechanism with a CCD-certified merge step guarantees penetration-free results. Experiments demonstrate stable convergence, non-penetration, and near-linear scaling on large-scale contact-rich scenes (thousands of bodies, tens of millions of triangles) across multiple nodes.
